newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian ports handled 227.13 mln T cargo in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Indian ports handled 227.13 mln T cargo in 1996/97.

text.p: Major Indian ports handled 227.13 million tonnes of cargo in 1996/97 (April-March) against a target of 215 million tonnes, the Surface Transport Ministry said on Monday.
"Ten of the eleven ports exceeded their targets during the financial year," the ministry said in a statement.
Only the Marmugao port in the western state of Goa fell short of its target, handling 10.4 million tonnes of cargo in 1996/97 against a target of 12.5 million tonnes.
Vishakapatnam port in southeastern India handled 34.5 million tonnes of cargo in 1996/97, the highest amount handled by any major port so far, the statement said.
Kandla port and Bombay port in western India each handled 33.71 million tonnes of cargo in 1996/97, the statement added. It gave no details regarding the other ports.
